page: Google Cloud Platform c4-standard-16-lssd is a general-purpose virtual machine instance powered by an Intel Xeon 6985P-C processor. Built on the x86_64 architecture, this instance features 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 8 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The processor operates at a base frequency of 2.3 GHz and is equipped with a 504 MB L3 cache. Memory configuration includes 60.0 GB of RAM, translating to 3.75 GB per core. For local storage, the instance is bundled with 539 GB of NVMe SSD capacity distributed across two local drives, while it includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data indicates strong single-core efficiency, with the instance achieving top-tier performance in single-threaded gzip compression at 36.82 GB/sec and single-threaded bzip3 decompression at 15.64 GB/sec. Geekbench single-core and text processing scores also rank in the top tier. Multi-core and memory performance fall within the average range, as demonstrated by a stress-ng multi-core CPU score of 18,700.11 and a large-block memory read bandwidth of 132.61 GB/sec. Large-block memory write bandwidth is recorded at 56.89 GB/sec. For database operations, the instance handles 34.1 million Redis SET operations per second and scores 9,335.54 on PassMark database operations, both placing in the average tier.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the c4-standard-16-lssd offers a balanced resource density, combining dedicated compute cores with high-speed local NVMe storage. The inclusion of local SSDs provides low-latency storage access, making it suitable for database workloads, caching layers, and web serving. However, the 3.75 GB of RAM per core may present a bottleneck for memory-intensive applications, and the lack of a GPU limits its utility for heavy machine learning training, though it maintains average performance for small and medium LLM inference tasks. Appropriate workloads include relational databases, software compilation, static web serving, and text processing pipelines.
